articles.title: Silverstein Adds 55K SF of Leases at Downtown L.A.’s U.S. Bank Tower
articles.narrative: Silverstein Properties has secured over 55,000 square feet of new and expanded office leases at the U.S. Bank Tower in Downtown Los Angeles. The transactions include an expansion by a prominent injury law firm, a full-floor lease by an engineering and design firm, a new headquarters for the Los Angeles Area Chamber of Commerce, and a relocation for a consultant firm. These deals contribute to over 145,000 square feet of leasing activity at the tower in the past year, exceeding the landlord's expectations following a $60 million upgrade.

data_points.notable_features: One of the tallest buildings west of the Mississippi River, recently underwent a $60 million upgrade.

articles.title: Manhattan’s Supply of New Condos Expected to Deepen in Q4: Report
articles.narrative: Manhattan's new development condo market experienced a significant dip in the third quarter of 2026, with real supply 28 percent below its 10-year average and new contract signings down 27 percent year-over-year. However, analysts predict a substantial increase in pipeline supply for the fourth quarter, with 3,796 units in the pipeline, a 40 percent rise from the previous year. This anticipated influx of new projects, particularly in undersupplied residential areas, is expected to alleviate the current low inventory and stabilize the market, with a focus on units priced around $2,000 per square foot.

people.name: Jason Thomas
people.title: Senior Vice President of Research and Market Analytics

articles.market_intelligence: Manhattan's real supply of condo development units in Q3 2026 was 28% below its 10-year average. The pipeline supply for Q4 2026 is up 40% from last year. Q3 2026 new condo contracts signed in Manhattan declined 27% year-over-year. Contract dollar volume in Q3 2026 was $961 million, down 13% from last year. Brooklyn saw a 21% year-over-year decrease in new development contracts signed in Q3 2026, with $1.2 billion in sales volume year-to-date.

articles.title: Tishman Speyer Signs 150-Year Ground Lease to Reposition Chrysler Building
articles.narrative: Tishman Speyer has signed a 150-year ground lease for the iconic Chrysler Building in New York City, taking over stewardship from The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art, which owns the land. The agreement includes a commitment from Tishman Speyer to invest $235 million in renovations and upgrades to reposition the 77-story office tower. The repositioning strategy will focus on converting a significant portion of vacant space into pre-built office suites to attract new tenants, addressing the building's high vacancy rate and aiming to revitalize its market presence.

data_points.address: 405 Lexington Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Landmarked 77-story office tower; repositioning plans include converting 75% of vacant space into pre-built office suites.
data_points.project_notes: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art evicted previous leaseholder RFR Holding in November 2024 due to default on ground-rent payments. The new ground lease is for 150 years.

articles.title: John Meko of WiredScore: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: WiredScore's latest report, "Fit for lease: How digital connectivity became the new test for Class A offices," reveals that 81% of tenants prefer office suites with pre-installed connectivity. The report highlights a significant gap between tenant expectations and reality, as only one in four tenants has operational connectivity on their lease start date. John Meko, WiredScore's VP for North America, notes that tenants increasingly view connectivity as a fundamental utility and are willing to sign longer leases for superior service, with 89% stating they would not renew due to poor connectivity. WiredScore, acquired by Meter in February 2026, is addressing this by speculatively installing internet infrastructure in office buildings to provide a turnkey solution for tenants and streamline the move-in process for landlords.

articles.title: Health Care Investment Firm Lorient Inks 6K-SF lease at Durst’s 825 Third Avenue
articles.narrative: Lorient, a healthcare investment firm, has signed a 5,556-square-foot lease for its inaugural New York City office at 825 Third Avenue in Midtown East. The Durst Organization, which owns the 40-story office tower, represented itself in the transaction, while Lee & Associates represented Lorient. The building recently underwent a $150 million renovation, enhancing its appeal with modern amenities and prebuilt, furnished suites for immediate occupancy.

data_points.address: 825 Third Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The building recently underwent a $150 million renovation, adding a 6,000-square-foot wrap-around terrace, cafe, wine bar, lounge, and conference space. The leased space is a "DurstReady suite," which is prebuilt, furnished, and equipped for immediate occupancy.

articles.market_intelligence: The average asking rent for Class A office space in Midtown was $85.08 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026.

articles.title: Agora Realty Breaks Ground on Final Phase of $375M Mixed-Use Entertainment Project in North Las Vegas
articles.narrative: Agora Realty has commenced the third and final phase of Hylo Park, a substantial mixed-use entertainment development in North Las Vegas. This $375 million phase, spanning 25 acres, will introduce a 250,000-square-foot indoor multi-sport field house, an existing multi-sport arena, a college preparatory sports academy, outdoor public spaces, retail, restaurants, a family entertainment center, and a 177-key Hilton Embassy Suites. The project is expected to be completed in late 2027, building on previous phases that included a grocery-anchored retail center and a residential neighborhood.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a multi-sport indoor field house, multi-sport arena, college preparatory sports academy, and a Hilton Embassy Suites.
data_points.project_notes: This is the third and final phase of a 73-acre mixed-use entertainment project. Previous phases included Hylo Park South, a 90,750-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center completed in July 2026, and The West End, a nearly 400-home residential neighborhood developed by Lennar Corp.

articles.title: Affinius Capital Provides s $94.8M Construction Loan for Student Housing Project Near Oregon State University
articles.narrative: Affinius Capital has provided a $94.8 million construction loan for Zev Corvallis, a 13-story student housing development near Oregon State University. The project, developed by Fields Holdings, will offer 667 beds across 262 units and is slated for completion in fall 2028. The property will feature a comprehensive amenity package and 4,500 square feet of retail space.

data_points.notable_features: 13-story building with a pool, rooftop deck, indoor basketball court, sauna, theater, fitness center, yoga room, study and resident lounges, and 4,500 square feet of retail space.
data_points.project_notes: Residences will be furnished with quartz countertops, stainless steel appliances, modern cabinetry, in-unit washers/dryers and smart-home technology.

articles.title: Hines Acquires 99 West Paces Apartments in Atlanta for $240M
articles.narrative: Hines Global Income Trust Inc. (HGIT) has acquired 99 West Paces, a 312-unit luxury apartment tower in Atlanta's Buckhead district. The property, built in 2023, was 95 percent occupied at the time of sale and was reportedly purchased for approximately $240 million. This acquisition marks Hines' entry into the Atlanta market and is part of a larger $500 million investment by HGIT across multiple cities.

data_points.address: 99 West Paces Ferry Road, Atlanta, GA
data_points.notable_features: Luxury apartment tower with a wellness club, fitness center, pet spa, coworking spaces, and a sky lounge, located within walking distance to retail and entertainment.

articles.title: Miami Design District Associates, BH3 Partner to Develop 20-Story Office Building
articles.narrative: Miami Design District Associates and BH3 Management have formed a joint venture to develop The Ursa, a 20-story Class A office tower in Miami's Design District. The project will feature 250,000 square feet of office space, 15,000 square feet of ground-level retail, and onsite parking. This newly formed partnership has expanded the project's original vision by 40 percent, with construction slated to begin in 2027 and completion expected in 2029.

data_points.notable_features: 20-story tower with 14-foot ceilings, amenity deck, art installations, and fitness facilities.
data_points.project_notes: Project's original vision expanded by 40 percent with the formation of the new joint venture. Construction expected to begin in 2027.

articles.title: Northmarq Provides $68.8M Agency Loan for Refinancing of Texas Multifamily Portfolio
articles.narrative: Northmarq has provided a $68.8 million Freddie Mac loan for the refinancing of a three-property multifamily portfolio in Texas. The portfolio consists of 940 units across two properties in Houston, Holden Heights and Estancia San Miguel, and one property in San Antonio, The Montecristo. The fixed-rate loan was originated on behalf of Francis Property Management.

data_points.project_notes: The portfolio includes Holden Heights (282 units, built 2015), Estancia San Miguel (300 units, built 2006), and The Montecristo (358 units, built 2005).

articles.title: Berkadia closes sale of 228-unit multifamily property in Madison market
articles.narrative: Berkadia has facilitated the sale of Aster at Sun Prairie, a 228-unit multifamily property in Sun Prairie, Wisconsin. The transaction involved Continental Properties as the seller and Weidner Apartment Homes as the buyer. The property, built in 2018, offers direct-access units and a range of amenities, benefiting from its location in a rapidly growing area of the Madison metro.

data_points.notable_features: 100% direct-access units, luxury clubhouse with swimming pool and fitness center, 1:1 garage parking, walkable suburban location surrounded by grocery, restaurants, and major retailers. Located on the rapidly expanding east side of the Madison metro, near American Family Insurance headquarters, American Center Business Park, and UW Health’s East Side Medical Campus.

articles.title: Cushman & Wakefield adds managing director in Detroit office
articles.narrative: Cushman & Wakefield has appointed Mike Valant as Managing Director in its Detroit office. Valant brings 15 years of commercial real estate experience, specializing in cross-market leasing and dispositions across various property types including office, industrial, investment, and retail sectors. His expertise spans complex transactions for both tenants and landlords, as well as buyers and sellers.

articles.title: Stream Realty Partners negotiates 63,409-square-foot office lease in Lisle
articles.narrative: Sentinel Technologies has signed a full-building lease for 63,409 square feet at Corporetum Office Campus X in Lisle, IL, relocating its headquarters from Downers Grove. The move, which marks the company's first headquarters relocation in over 30 years, will consolidate its office, R&D, and technology lab functions. The building will undergo significant capital improvements to support Sentinel's long-term occupancy.

data_points.notable_features: Four-story building located in Chicago's East/West Corridor along Interstate 88, offering prominent visibility and signage opportunities.
data_points.project_notes: Sentinel Technologies is expected to relocate in Q1 2027. The building will undergo significant capital improvements as part of the new lease.

articles.title: Fort Worth’s Trademark Property Company closes financing on four development projects across Texas
articles.narrative: Trademark Property Company has closed financing on four development and redevelopment projects across Texas, totaling over 830,000 square feet of retail space with a combined value of $417 million. These projects include the redevelopment of Lincoln Square into Anthem in Arlington, the construction of Shivers Farm in Southlake, and Dunham Pointe in Cypress, along with the acquisition of Oak Hill Plaza in Austin. The activity reflects a positive shift in the retail real estate market, characterized by low national vacancy rates and investor interest in new retail development, particularly grocery-anchored centers.
articles.market_intelligence: National retail vacancy held at 4.4% in Q2 2026, well below the 7.4% historical average. New retail construction remains scarce nationally. Dallas, Houston, and Austin account for 21% of the current national construction pipeline. In JLL’s June 2026 U.S. retail report, 48% of investors stated they were interested in investing in new retail development in 2026. Malls are outperforming all commercial property sectors with values up 13%.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap brokers sale of 44,068-square-foot shopping center in Temple
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of Legends Plaza, a 44,068-square-foot shopping center in Temple, Texas. Both the buyer and seller were private investors. The buyer intends to continue operating the property as a multi-tenant retail center.

data_points.notable_features: Located along Loop 363; formerly a grocery store redeveloped into a multi-tenant shopping center.

articles.title: Intracorp Lands $173M Loan for Austin Condo Project
articles.narrative: Intracorp has secured a $173 million construction loan from BGO to begin development on Leland South Congress, a 265-unit condominium project in Austin, TX. The development will also include nearly 22,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a 6,000-square-foot outdoor dining paseo. The project is a joint effort with co-developer Leifer Properties and partners Northland Properties and Aron Industries, with completion anticipated in 2029.

data_points.notable_features: Includes nearly 22,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space and a 6,000-square-foot outdoor dining paseo.
data_points.project_notes: The site previously housed a gas station, auto shop, nursing and rehab center, and parking lot, all of which have been demolished.

articles.title: Kidder Mathews Arranges Sale of 58K-SF Tacoma Industrial Building
articles.narrative: Kidder Mathews has facilitated the sale of the Smith-Western Building, a 58,255-square-foot industrial distribution facility in Tacoma, Washington. The property, fully leased to a long-term tenant through 2031, was sold amidst challenging market conditions characterized by high interest rates and elevated industrial vacancy. The transaction highlights the value of stabilized assets with established tenancy in the current market.

data_points.notable_features: Concrete industrial property with 24-foot clear height, nine dock-high doors, two grade-level doors, three exterior levelers, and a secure fenced yard with outside storage.

articles.title: Henricksen Unveils New Headquarters in Illinois
articles.narrative: Henricksen, a national contract furniture dealer, has opened its new 14,000-square-foot headquarters in Oak Brook, Illinois. This move from Itasca, Illinois, is a strategic decision to support hybrid work models, improve collaboration, and enhance client engagement. The new location was chosen for its central access to Chicago and major expressways, reflecting a focus on optimizing space and design for modern work patterns.

data_points.notable_features: Full-floor renovated space designed to support hybrid work patterns and enhance collaboration.
data_points.project_notes: Strategic shift from previous headquarters in Itasca, IL.

articles.title: Janus Living Pays $123.5M for Greensboro Senior Living Center
articles.narrative: Janus Living has acquired Harmony at Greensboro, a 174-unit senior living community in Greensboro, NC, for $123.5 million. The facility, which offers independent, assisted, and memory care units along with rehabilitation services, was sold by Smith/Packett. Smith/Packett will continue to operate the center, which opened in March 2020. This acquisition marks Janus Living's entry into the North Carolina market.

data_points.notable_features: Offers independent, assisted, and memory care residential units, as well as onsite rehabilitation services.
data_points.project_notes: Construction started in 2018 and the center opened in March 2020. The original construction cost was $38 million.

articles.title: Local Investor Pays $30M For Block 37 In Heart Of Downtown Chicago
articles.narrative: Edwards Realty Co. has acquired Block 37, a 278,000-square-foot vertical shopping mall in downtown Chicago, for $30 million. The local investor purchased the property at a significant discount, with plans to reposition the large retail asset.

data_points.notable_features: Vertical shopping mall in downtown Chicago.

articles.title: Activist Investor Buys Stake In Empire State Building Owner
articles.narrative: Erez Asset Management, led by Bruce Schanzer, has acquired a 5.8% stake in the REIT that owns the iconic Empire State Building. This move by the activist investor signals potential future engagement with the REIT's management regarding its strategy or operations.

articles.title: Soaring Yields Strand REITs In M&A No-Man’s-Land
articles.narrative: Rising 10-Year Treasury yields, now exceeding 5%, are creating significant challenges for REITs in the M&A market. This surge in yields is necessitating real-time repricing of deals, effectively stalling large-scale transactions. The current economic environment has placed many potential acquisitions on hold as REITs navigate the increased cost of capital.

articles.title: San Francisco Office Market Climbs, Fueling Demand For Large Blocks, Luxury Space
articles.narrative: The San Francisco office market has experienced a significant surge in leasing activity during 2026, driven primarily by demand from artificial intelligence companies. This robust performance has led to 12.1 million square feet of office space being leased year-to-date, indicating strong demand for large blocks and luxury office accommodations in the market.
